channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: Hokkaido potato growers harvest their best crop in a decade
item.description: After a punishing summer hurt crops elsewhere in Japan, Hokkaido's potato farmers are celebrating their best harvest in a decade. A favorable balance of rain and temperature helped the island, which supplies about 80 percent of Japan's potatoes, produce an especially strong crop.

item.title: Texas school honors beloved longtime custodian 'Miss Marilyn'
item.description: A new Texas elementary school has been named for Marilyn Hampton, a 76-year-old custodian who spent 39 years caring for students and staff. Beyond cleaning, 'Miss Marilyn' bought supplies, tutored children and found football tickets for families; she still helps at an early-learning center.

item.title: Farmer turns a stray exam-phone-number mix-up into student pep talks
item.description: A Chinese strawberry farmer discovered his phone number had appeared in a national exam passage when students began calling. For more than a decade he has answered with encouragement instead of annoyance; one caller later reached a top Beijing university and finally met him over Peking duck.

item.title: A Rembrandt fan leaves the museum wearing the master’s art
item.description: The Rembrandt House Museum revived its “Poor Man’s Rembrandt” pop-up, where noted tattoo artist Henk Schiffmacher inks designs based on the painter’s drawings. An AP reporter chose a wide-eyed 1630 self-portrait for a permanent, portable piece of museum art.

item.title: The “Picasso of Pumpkin Carvers” marks 40 years of gourd art
item.description: Mike Valladao, a systems engineer better known as Farmer Mike, celebrated four decades of sculpting giant pumpkins at Half Moon Bay’s festival. His creatures, landscapes and pop-culture figures can weigh hundreds of pounds—and last only a few days.

item.title: The rubber duck’s surprisingly deep American history
item.description: The familiar bath toy evolved from heavy vulcanized-rubber forms into Elenore Shannahan’s floating 1931 design and Peter Ganine’s 1947 vinyl duck. Along the way it inspired a hit song, entered the National Toy Hall of Fame and even helped scientists model ocean currents.

item.title: Divers rescue a kangaroo more than a mile from shore
item.description: A South Australian dive crew found an exhausted juvenile kangaroo roughly three kilometers out in Boston Bay. They lifted it through the boat's water door, let it rest aboard and later watched it hop away from the beach under its own strength.

item.title: An anonymous diner buys lunch for 27 disabled residents and caregivers
item.description: A stranger at an Incheon barbecue restaurant added premium beef to a community group's order and quietly paid the entire $420 bill. The outing included disabled residents, staff and volunteers from a local welfare center.

item.title: Plant-inspired filter begins catching microplastics in Atlantic City wastewater
item.description: A commercial-scale device designed by Princeton alumni mimics water-shedding plants while attracting plastic particles. An Atlantic City utility began a two-year pilot after laboratory prototypes removed 98% of microplastics from wastewater.

item.title: A wrong turn puts a stranger in time to save a foster family from a fire
item.description: A driver's GPS mistake led him past a burning Georgia home, where he woke the family and helped everyone escape. James and Larita Burke, who have fostered about 500 children, got all 11 children and a grandchild out safely.

item.title: Six winless seasons cannot dampen a high-school baseball team's joy
item.description: Nova Scotia's Dartmouth Spartans have not won in six years, but the players keep returning for camaraderie and love of the game. The open-door team gives newcomers a chance to play without performance barriers.

item.title: New Amazon reserve helps a conservation group pass 70 million protected acres
item.description: A new 715,000-acre wildlife reserve along Bolivia's Iténez River protects a migration corridor for jaguars, river dolphins, giant otters and other species. The project pushed Rainforest Trust's total supported conservation past 70 million acres.

item.title: Tiny Scottish island uncovers evidence of a major medieval monastery
item.description: Residents of Lismore helped crowdfund excavations that found burials, carved crosses, buildings and more than 1,000 traces of precious-metal work. The discoveries show the island’s early monastery was a major center of worship, craftsmanship and learning.

item.title: Six new calves lift Cambodia’s endangered river-dolphin population
item.description: A successful breeding season added six Irrawaddy dolphin calves along a 75-mile stretch of the Mekong, bringing the local population to 118. Community conservation efforts are helping protect an animal regarded as sacred in Cambodian and Laotian traditions.

item.title: New Yorker named Service cleans an illegal dumping site himself
item.description: After reporting a pile of trash beneath a Brooklyn rail bridge, Joshua Service took commenters’ advice and returned with gloves and a rake. He filled 10 bags in two hours, prompting a city council member to honor him at the site.
